cohort: The cohort consisted of 90 nulliparous women with singleton cephalic pregnancies at 37-40 weeks gestation, cervical dilation >= 3 cm, and no prior LSCS or abnormal cardiotocography.
finding: Serial intrapartum ultrasound measurements, specifically AOP >= 120 degrees and PD >= 2.7 cm at >= 6 cm cervical dilation, are predictive of vaginal delivery, with the change in AOP (delta AOP > 10 degrees) being the most accurate predictor.
mod_finding: Intrapartum ultrasound measurements, particularly AOP and PD and the change in AOP, are predictive of vaginal delivery and can help reduce unnecessary caesarean deliveries.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken twice during the first stage of labor, once at recruitment (cervical dilation >= 3 cm) and again 3-5 hours later.
